def: A label, binary or graded, saying how well a document answers a query's information need; a set of them is called qrels.
The fraction of the first k results that are relevant.
The fraction of all relevant documents that appear in the first k results.
The share of queries for which at least one relevant document appears in the top k, also called success at k.
The average over queries of 1 divided by the rank of the first relevant result, so only the first hit counts.
For one query, the mean of the precision at each relevant result's rank, divided by the total number of relevant documents so missed ones count as zeros.
Mean average precision: the average of average precision over all queries in a test set.
Discounted cumulative gain: the sum of each result's gain divided by log2(rank + 1), so good results count less the lower they sit.
Normalised DCG: DCG divided by the DCG of the ideal ordering, giving a 0 to 1 score that can be averaged across queries.
Judgements with several levels, such as 0 to 3, so that perfect answers can be told apart from marginal ones.
A retrieved document that no judge labelled, conventionally scored as non-relevant, which can under-score systems that retrieve differently.
